For 5,000 years, one productive beef cow has been worth about one ounce of gold.

Mesopotamia. Rome. The Viking Age. The ratio held.

In 1926, a good cow cost $22. A $20 gold coin held 0.9675 ounces of gold. Almost exactly one ounce per cow.

Today, a young productive beef cow sells for $4,000 to $5,000 at auction. Gold sits around $4,500 an ounce.

The ratio has held for five millennia, and still holds today.

Harnesses often get dismissed as just scaffolding, just prompt engineering, and not real research. But that couldn't be farther from the truth. The same model weights that score 30% on ARC-AGI score 95% with a better harness.

So we gathered a group of researchers and founders working at the frontier to do a deep dive into the state of harnesses. 

We cover how we got to this point, the case for making your harness as expressive as possible, and what YC learned building an agent for every employee in the company.

ok hear me out

as the raw material gets cheaper, the signature gets more expensive.

AI is going to make 95% of knowledge work cheap af. 

which means the remaining 5%, the people who actually know something weird, useful, non-obvious, are going to get priced like luxury goods.

payouts won’t be a linear “this person is 2x better so pay them 2x.” that are tracked against input labour.

more like “there are 3 people in the world I trust to get this done, and I want them”

and yes, obviously, just like they make their bags in China, you’ll be cooking stuff on Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, whatever.

but that is not the point.

the point is whether people know that you know what to ask, what trends to ignore, what smells wrong, what matters, and when to bet against the obvious answer. 

so….if that’s you, you should probably think less like a knowledge worker and more like a luxury fashion brand.

scarcity. taste. provenance. trust. selective access. ridiculous pricing.

unironically, become Hermès 🤡🤡🤡

candidates.text:
One way to think about agents is that whatever you left unspecified is a free variable for your agent to change.

So if you ask "make the code faster", it can tweak code readability, security, durability, etc. to achieve this goal. What it ends up doing is determined by its training priors and context it finds itself in. Upon extreme pressure, it will actively degrade the underspecified or non-evaluated.

Practically this means that for anything underspecified, you're importing default choices that OpenAI/Anthropic made during their model training into your own work, and remember that their choices are largely dependent on what can be measured and rewarded during RL runs.

candidates.text:
AI HACK

Here’s a trick I stumbled upon. 

Invite your AIs meet in a Slack channel and coordinate: GPT, Grok Bot, and Claude. 

Grok is the point guard - it has agents monitoring and doing dispatch. 

It keeps me informed. 

GPT Astra is the mastermind. It tells Claude what to do. 

Claude runs the browser. 

GPT tells Claude what to do in the slack channel. Claude reports back.

I needed to set this up because Astra has browser take-over limitations. 

Now it does not have that b/c Claude reports back what it sees to GPT. 

I guess you could call it an ‘AI Working Session’. 

AIs have different strengths. You can have fun with this.
